result.topic_en: Riemann discusses the dependence of gas pressure on density, starting from the Mariotte (Boyle) and Gay-Lussac laws, derives the adiabatic law log p = -k log v + const from the heat quantity expressed with the two specific heats, mentions experiments by Regnault, Joule and Thomson, and adds side calculations of second derivatives of a double integral.

methods.what: Combined Boyle–Mariotte and Gay-Lussac ideal gas law in logarithmic form
Heat absorbed expressed via specific heats at constant pressure and volume
Adiabatic condition (no heat exchange) gives differential relation
Poisson adiabatic law with constant ratio of specific heats
Mayer's relation: mechanical equivalent of heat gives difference of specific heats
Hyperbolic PDE with boundary conditions and its integration (Riemann-function type calculation)

items.quote:
Nach [-...-] Versuchen von Regnault, Joule und Thomson sind diese Gesetze für Sauerstoff, Stickstoff, Wasserstoff und

items.english: According to experiments by Regnault, Joule and Thomson these laws are probably very nearly valid for oxygen, nitrogen, hydrogen and their mixtures under all producible pressures and temperatures.

items.quote:
Man muß daher [-lieber-] für diese Abhängigkeit das Gesetz zu Grunde legen, nach welchem sich der Druck eines Gases
mit der Dichtigkeit ändert, wenn das Gas keine Wärme aufnimmt oder abgiebt.
items.english: One must therefore base this dependence on the law by which the pressure of a gas changes with density when the gas neither absorbs nor gives off heat.
